attributes.x-qa-platform-provenance: REDUCED KEYCLOAK REALM EXPORT (26.0.8), not hand-written. Configured via kcadm.sh, exported with `kc.sh export --users same_file`, then stripped of every key that only restated a Keycloak default -- notably components['org.keycloak.keys.KeyProvider'], which would have committed the realm's private signing key. Do not paste it back.
attributes.x-qa-platform-docs: Rendered by the Helm chart's keycloak-realm-secret.yaml, which carries the full rationale; the placeholders below are substituted at template time. This file cannot carry JSON comments: an unrecognised top-level key such as `_comment` aborts import with 'Unrecognized field ... RealmRepresentation, not marked as ignorable'. This `attributes` map is the one place a note fits.
attributes.x-qa-platform-tenant-claim: The tenant-id protocol mapper must emit a UUID: oidc-authn-plugin parses it with Uuid::parse_str. The value is toolkit_security::constants::DEFAULT_TENANT_ID, which owns every row created while auth_disabled was true. Changing it hides that data silently rather than erroring.
attributes.x-qa-platform-dev-only: DEV FIXTURE. The seeded users' passwords are in this file in the clear -- admin/AdminPass1! and viewer/ViewerPass1!, not admin/admin and viewer/viewer any more. MEASURED: the realm's own passwordPolicy (below) is enforced by --import-realm itself, not only on a future change, so importing the old admin/admin credential (equal to its own username, with no digit/uppercase/special character) made Keycloak abort start-up with invalidPasswordMinSpecialCharsMessage rather than import a realm that violates its own policy. Not a template for a real deployment. The `users` array below is now wrapped in `{{if .Values.devMode}}...{{end}}` -- keycloak-realm-secret.yaml's `tpl` call expands it same as any other placeholder here -- so these two well-known-literal-password application users only render at all when the installer has explicitly said this is a throwaway stand; a real install gets an empty `users` array and neither login exists. `check_realm_secrecy.py` asserts both sides of that. directAccessGrantsEnabled is now OFF on qa-platform-ui -- see that client's own comment -- so getting a token without a browser means the qa-platform-workflow service-account client's client-credentials grant, not a password grant against a public client.

passwordPolicy: length(8) and notUsername and notEmail and lowerCase(1) and upperCase(1) and digits(1) and specialChars(1)

attributes.x-qa-platform-direct-grants: OFF, deliberately. This is a PUBLIC client (no client secret), so a resource-owner-password-credentials grant here would accept a username/password directly from any caller that can reach the token endpoint -- no PKCE, no redirect URI, no origin check, none of the standardFlow protections above. The browser-facing standardFlowEnabled/PKCE path is the only login route for this client; an automated caller that needs a token without a browser uses the qa-platform-workflow service-account client's client-credentials grant instead.
